subject: physics
question_text: What is inertia? What gives the measure of inertia?

verification.note: Sri Chaitanya IPE Junior Fastrack (Rev. May 2024), Unit 5 VERY SHORT ANSWER. The 1+1 mark split is invented and needs a Telangana IPE teacher; no exam appearance years are printed for this question, so appearances[] stays empty. AP appearance: asked on the AP Inter 1st-year Physics paper, March 2026 (the first paper of the new 85-mark NCERT pattern) — transcription evidence, claim until the official paper PDF confirms the question number.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What inertia is
lines: Inertia is the inability of a body to
change its state of rest or of uniform
steps.margin_note: The phrase "by itself" is the whole idea — do not drop it.
steps.why: A body does not resist motion; it resists a CHANGE of motion. Nothing about its state changes until an outside force acts.
common_mistakes: Calling inertia a force. It is a property of the body, not a force acting on it.

recall.must_convey: That inertia is the inability of a body to change its own state of rest or of uniform motion.
accept: inability to change its state by itself
a body cannot change rest or motion on its own
body tanaka tanuga state change cheyyaledu
reject: mass is the measure of inertia

steps.memory_tip: Inertia resists CHANGE of state, not motion itself. Keep the word "change" in the sentence.

steps.label: What measures it
lines: Mass is the measure of inertia.

lines.text: Larger the mass, larger the inertia.

steps.margin_note: The second mark is for naming MASS. Say the word plainly.
steps.why: The same push changes a light body much more than a heavy one, so mass is exactly the quantity being measured.
common_mistakes: Answering "weight". Weight changes from place to place; inertia does not.

recall.must_convey: That mass is the measure of inertia.
accept: mass is the measure of inertia

steps.memory_tip: The measure is mass — more mass, more resistance to the same force.
